title: Rollout approvals RBAC matrix (Dedicated staged rollouts)
content:
Last updated: 2025-02-21 (Kaitlyn)

Context
- Project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
- This sheet defines: who can create/edit rollout plans, who can approve stage advancement, who can abort/rollback, and who can view/export audit events.
- Applies to Dedicated pools only (hosted/shared not in scope for v1).

Principles / assumptions
1) Tenant isolation: enterprise tenant actors can only affect resources within their tenant (tenant_id boundary) and only allowlisted pools.
2) Separation of duties (recommended, not hard requirement for v1): the person who edits a plan should not be the sole approver for production stages.
3) Least privilege: customer roles do not get “operator override” or break-glass actions.
4) Everything is auditable: create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold are audit events (see ADR-028).
5) Fail-safe defaults: missing metrics => evaluator puts rollout in HOLD; releasing HOLD is treated as an approval action (manual).

Glossary
- RolloutPlan: versioned plan (plan_version increments on update).
- Stage: a step with traffic weight + evaluation window + gates + approval policy.
- Approval: a stage-level action to advance (or to release a HOLD, depending on state machine).
- Abort: stop rollout; optionally trigger rollback policy (implementation-specific).
- Operator: Redwood internal actor (employee/service account) acting on behalf of ops.
- Tenant actor: customer identity scoped to tenant_id (SSO/SAML user or service account).

Permission primitives (proposed strings used by APIs)
| Permission | Description | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| rollout.view | Read rollout plans + current state for pools you can access | Console list/detail pages |
| rollout.edit | Create/update rollout plans and stages/gates | Does NOT allow approve/abort |
| rollout.approve | Approve stage advancement / release HOLD | Includes “approve to proceed” for Stage >= 1 |
| rollout.abort | Abort rollout (stop + optional rollback) | Treated as high-risk |
| rollout.override | Operator-only overrides (e.g., bypass gate, force weight) | Internal only; gated by break-glass |
| audit.view | View audit events in Console | Filtered by tenant/pool |
| audit.export | Export audit events to external sink (SIEM) | Typically security/compliance |

Resource scopes (enforced server-side)
| Resource | Scope key(s) | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Dedicated pool | tenant_id + pool_id | tenant actors cannot cross tenant_id; internal can access per internal policy |
| RolloutPlan | tenant_id + pool_id + rollout_plan_id | plan_id unique per pool |
| Audit event stream | tenant_id (+ pool_id optional) | export access restricted |

Internal Redwood roles (human)
- NOTE: these are “role bundles” mapped to permissions above. Final mapping lives in auth config.

| Internal role | Typical people | Intended use |
|---|---|---|
| Platform Operator | SRE on-call, Dedicated ops | Day-2 operations: pause/abort during incidents, approve when gates pass |
| Release Manager | release engineering | Coordinating rollouts during release trains |
| Platform Engineer | platform/control plane/routing engineers | Create/edit plans; may approve in non-prod; prod approvals discouraged |
| Support Escalation | support lead (internal) | View state + audit for debugging; no approvals |
| Security Auditor | security/compliance | Audit view/export; no ability to alter rollout |

Enterprise tenant roles (customer)
| Tenant role | Typical customer title | Intended use |
|---|---|---|
| Tenant Viewer | engineer, analyst | Read-only visibility |
| Tenant Operator | platform/SRE on customer side | Approve/abort within tenant scope (if enabled) |
| Tenant Admin | admin/owner | Manage plan edits + approvals (for opt-in tenants) |
| Tenant Security Auditor | GRC/security | Audit view/export; no changes |

TABLE A — Internal role → permissions matrix
Legend: Y = allowed by default, N = not allowed, (C) = conditional / requires extra checks

| Action / permission | Platform Operator | Release Manager | Platform Engineer | Support Escalation | Security Auditor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| rollout.view | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y |
| rollout.edit | (C) | (C) | Y | N | N |
| rollout.approve | Y | Y | (C) | N | N |
| rollout.abort | Y | Y | (C) | N | N |
| rollout.override | (C) | (C) | (C) | N | N |
| audit.view | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y |
| audit.export | N | N | N | N | (C) |

Condition notes (Internal)
- rollout.edit for Platform Operator / Release Manager: allowed in emergencies, but expected path is Platform Engineer authors plan + Operator approves. We may enforce via policy later (e.g., “two-person rule”) but v1 is guidance + audit.
- rollout.approve for Platform Engineer: allowed in dev/staging; in prod requires explicit “oncall override” or membership in Operator group.
- rollout.abort: requires pool access and (for prod) justification string in request (stored in audit event).
- rollout.override: INTERNAL ONLY; requires break-glass + short TTL session + audit event contains reason + incident link.
- audit.export: only Security Auditor (and service accounts) should have this by default; requests are logged.

TABLE B — Enterprise tenant role → permissions matrix
NOTE: for v1, enterprise tenant actions are behind allowlist (per-tenant feature flag) and per-pool enablement.

| Action / permission | Tenant Viewer | Tenant Operator | Tenant Admin | Tenant Security Auditor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| rollout.view | Y | Y | Y | Y |
| rollout.edit | N | N | (C) | N |
| rollout.approve | N | (C) | (C) | N |
| rollout.abort | N | (C) | (C) | N |
| rollout.override | N | N | N | N |
| audit.view | Y | Y | Y | Y |
| audit.export | N | N | (C) | (C) |

Condition notes (Enterprise)
- All (C) permissions require:
  - Tenant is allowlisted for Dedicated staged rollouts (feature flag).
  - Pool is enabled for customer-managed approvals.
  - User has completed SSO + (if configured) MFA.
  - Requests include an “approval_comment” / “abort_reason” (stored in audit event for compliance).
- rollout.edit for Tenant Admin is optional per tenant contract; default is Redwood-managed plans. If enabled, edits are constrained by guardrails (e.g., stage weights must sum to 100, evaluation windows bounded, gate types limited to supported set).
- audit.export for tenants requires explicit enablement + destination validation (SIEM integration path handled separately).

TABLE C — Environment restrictions
| Permission | dev | staging | prod |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| rollout.edit (internal) | Y | Y | Y |
| rollout.approve (internal) | Y | Y | (C) |
| rollout.abort (internal) | Y | Y | (C) |
| rollout.override (internal) | Y | (C) | (C) |
| rollout.approve/abort (tenant) | N | (C) | (C) |

Prod conditions (internal)
- Operator group membership required for approve/abort in prod pools.
- override in prod requires: incident_id OR change_request_id + break-glass.

TABLE D — API endpoints → required permission(s)
(For Eng reference; matches control plane + console backend endpoints)

| Endpoint (logical) | Operation | Required permission(s) |
|---|---|---|
| GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts | list plans + status | rollout.view |
| GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id} | get plan + stages | rollout.view |
| POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts | create plan | rollout.edit |
| PUT /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id} | update plan (new plan_version) | rollout.edit |
| POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id}:approve | approve stage / release hold | rollout.approve |
| POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id}:abort | abort rollout | rollout.abort |
| POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id}:override | bypass/force actions | rollout.override (internal only) |
| GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id}/audit | list audit events | audit.view |
| GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{plan_id}/audit:export | export audit events | audit.export |

TABLE E — Stage approval policy (recommended defaults)
(Used by Product/SRE to set sane defaults; not all fields are enforced by RBAC)

| Stage | Example weight | Approval requirement | Who can approve (default) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Stage 0 (shadow/internal) | 0% external | optional | internal only | can be used for warmup / canary probes |
| Stage 1 | 5% | manual | Platform Operator / Release Manager | require gates green for N minutes |
| Stage 2 | 25% | manual | Platform Operator / Release Manager | higher risk; watch queue depth |
| Stage 3 | 100% | manual | Platform Operator (preferred) | require explicit “finalize” comment |

Special cases
- Auto-hold state: evaluator can HOLD even after manual approval if gates fail. Releasing HOLD uses rollout.approve.
- Emergency abort: SRE Operator can abort immediately; follow-up incident process required.

Audit event requirements (summary)
- For each approve/abort/edit action, audit event must include:
  - actor_type (internal_user | tenant_user | service_account)
  - actor_id / email (where applicable)
  - tenant_id, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, plan_version
  - stage_id (if stage-scoped)
  - action (plan.create | plan.update | stage.approve | rollout.abort | rollout.hold.auto | rollout.override)
  - reason/comment (required for prod + tenant actions)
  - request_id / idempotency_key

Open questions / TODO
1) Do we enforce a hard two-person rule for prod (editor != approver) at policy layer, or ship as “best practice + audit” for v1?
2) Tenant Operator vs Tenant Admin: do we need both, or can we collapse to one role for beta?
3) Should Support Escalation have audit.view across all tenants by default, or only via time-bound elevation?
4) Should audit.export for enterprise be restricted to Tenant Security Auditor only (not Admin)?

Change log
- 2025-01-18: initial draft matrix (Kaitlyn)
- 2025-02-03: added audit.export + override permission separation (Marcus/Kevin feedback)
- 2025-02-12: clarified tenant allowlist conditions + required reason/comment fields (Sean/Rachel)
- 2025-02-21: added API endpoint mapping + environment restrictions table (Ethan/Chloe)
